judge.reason: Direct evidence of command injection via template literal in exec call with unsanitized query parameter.

description: The /tools/ping route uses exec with a template literal containing user input from req.query.host, allowing arbitrary command execution.
remediation: Use execFile or spawn with argument array, validate the host parameter against an allowlist of valid hosts.
title: Command Injection in /tools/ping via unsanitized host parameter

judge.reason: Direct evidence of command injection via string concatenation in childProcess.exec.

description: The runTool function uses child_process.exec with a concatenated user input from req.query.tool, allowing arbitrary command execution.
remediation: Use execFile or spawn with argument array, validate the tool parameter against a whitelist.
title: Command Injection in runTool via unsanitized tool parameter

judge.reason: Direct evidence of SQL injection via string concatenation in db.query.

description: The search function concatenates user input directly into a SQL query string, allowing arbitrary SQL injection.
evidence: db.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + term + "'");
remediation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements (e.g., db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?', [term])).
title: SQL Injection in search via unsanitized q parameter

judge.reason: Evidence shows an exposed debug endpoint '/debug-token' that leaks processed token data.

description: The /debug-token endpoint (defined in src/routes/search.js) computes and returns an MD5 digest of a hardcoded token. Debug endpoints should not be enabled in production as they can leak sensitive information.
evidence:
router.get("/debug-token", (req, res) => { const name = String(req.query.name ?? "fixture-user"); const digest = crypto.createHash("md5").update(fakeFixtureToken).digest("hex"); res.send(`

${name}

${digest}

`);
remediation: Remove or guard the /debug-token endpoint behind authentication, feature flags, or environment checks (e.g., only enable in development).
title: Debug Token Endpoint Exposed

judge.reason: Direct evidence of SQL injection via template literal in query string construction.

description: The /search route constructs a SQL query using a template literal with user input. While not immediately executed, the unsanitized input is a SQL injection vulnerability that could be exploited if the query is later used.
evidence: const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE display_name = '${term}'`;
remediation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements if the query is to be executed, or treat the input as untrusted and apply proper escaping.
title: SQL Injection in /search via unsanitized q parameter
